state_background_check.value: No — Texas's felony-disqualification requirement (Tex. Elec. Code § 141.001(a)(4)) applies only to "a public elective office in this state" by its own text, not federal office; separately, the U.S. Constitution's own qualifications for Congress (age, citizenship, residency) can't be added to by any state, so this doesn't reach U.S. House or Senate candidates either way
state_background_check.snippet: Tex. Elec. Code § 141.001: "(a) To be eligible to be a candidate for, or elected or appointed to, a public elective office in this state, a person must: ... (4) have not been finally convicted of a felony from which the person has not been pardoned or otherwise released from the resulting disabilities..." Congressional qualifications are set exclusively by the U.S. Constitution, confirmed per https://www.everycrsreport.com/reports/R41946.html: "the Framers intended the Constitution to be the exclusive source of qualifications for Members of Congress, and that the Framers thereby 'divested' States of any power to add qualifications."

enacted_laws.title: Maintaining American Superiority by Improving Export Control Transparency Act
enacted_laws.summary: Maintaining American Superiority by Improving Export Control Transparency Act This act requires the Department of Commerce's Bureau of Industry and Security (BIS) to annually report to Congress on export control licensing. Under current law, BIS administers and enforces controls on the export of dual-use goods (e.g., items with both civilian and military uses) and certain military parts and components. These export controls are implemented primarily under the Export Control Reform Act of 2018 (ECRA) through the Export Administration Regulations (EAR). Under this act, BIS must annually report to Congress on license applications, other requests for authorization, and end-use checks (on-site verifications conducted by BIS) for the export, reexport, release, and in-country transfer of items subject to the EAR to covered entities. A covered entity is any entity that (1) is located in a country listed in Country Group D:5 (countries that are identified by the Department of State as subject to U.S. arms embargoes), and (2) is included on the Entity List or the Military End-User List (two of the lists published by BIS containing information on the individuals, organizations, and addresses subject to restrictions involving items subject to the EAR). The act requires this report to include specified information, such as the name of the entity submitting the application, where the item is being exported, the decision with respect to the license application or authorization, and information on any end-use checks to ensure compliance with U.S. export controls. The information shall be exempt from public disclosure (except for aggregate statistics). Additionally, BIS must exclude from the report any information that could jeopardize an ongoing investigation.

bio_summary.value: Congressman Ronny Jackson proudly represents Texas’ 13th District, spanning 38 counties and over 40,000 square miles of the Panhandle and North Texas. A retired Navy Rear Admiral, White House Physician to three U.S. Presidents, and Chief Medical Advisor to President Donald J. Trump, Dr. Jackson spent 25 years serving our country with honor.

marital_status.snippet: He, his wife, and his children have been part of the fabric of this district for more than 30 years.

employment_record.snippet: Mark Nair is an educator, innovator, inventor, and entrepreneur running to be your voice in the United States House of Representatives.

platform.value: Stop AI integration into government until constitutional safeguards are in place, author legislation for Public AI, create non-partisan agency for AI oversight, ban government AI for facial recognition and surveillance, protect privacy by banning use of personal information to train AI, and require disclosure when AI is used in employment and other key decisions
platform.snippet: Currently, the administration is integrating AI into governmental systems. Until we create clear rules to safeguard our constitutional rights, this must STOP. That is why, as your next Congressman, I will work to implement AI policy that works for THE PEOPLE. I fully intend to author legislation that will fund Public AI that acts for our benefit and will institute a public, non-partisan agency for transparency, accountability, and sustainability. Providing universal access to AI tools and protecting our democratic principles is paramount. In the private sector, I will pursue effective and diligent anti-trust enforcement, limiting the power of corporate interests. In the public sector, I will seek to ban government AI tools for facial recognition and other surveillance, including analyzing your social media. We must hold surveillance accountable, and I will author comprehensive legislation that will protect privacy, including banning the use of personal information to train AI. This includes provisions so that people can disable AI access to their private data from their own devices. Further, following the example set by the California Legislature (SB 947-The No Robo Bosses Act of 2026), I will fight for a similar national policy. Employees must know when an AI is in the middle of decision making that affects their livelihoods.

platform.value: Fight for full transparency in medical costs and prices, work toward Medicare for All, and push for increased funding for rural hospitals and clinics
platform.snippet: Mark will change that. He'll fight for full transparency in medical costs and prices so you know what you're paying and why. He'll work toward Medicare for All, making healthcare costs fair, reasonable, and affordable for every American. He'll push for increased funding for our rural hospitals and clinics, facilities that have been cut to the bone and are disappearing from communities that need them most.

platform.value: Expand federal incentives for building affordable housing in underserved communities, restrict corporations from seizing single family homes, and protect renters from predatory companies
platform.snippet: Mark will fight to end it. He'll expand federal incentives for building affordable housing in underserved communities, restrict corporations from seizing single family homes, and protect renters from predatory companies.

platform.value: Push for campaign finance reform, strict ethics rules and full financial transparency for Congress, ban on stock trading in Congress, and real term limits
platform.snippet: Mark doesn't take corporate PAC money, and he never will. His only obligation is to you. He'll push for real campaign finance reform so billionaires can't buy elections anymore. He'll fight for strict ethics rules and full financial transparency for every member of Congress. He'll push for a ban on stock trading in Congress. And he'll push for real term limits, because no one should make a career out of public service while getting rich from it.

platform.value: Expand federal grants for water desalination and clean water infrastructure, and fund research and systems to replenish aquifers
platform.snippet: Mark will fight to keep water in the hands of the people who depend on it, not the corporations that exploit it. He'll expand federal grants for water desalination and clean water infrastructure. But he knows that solving this crisis long term means investing in the science and infrastructure to replenish our aquifers, not just manage their decline. That means funding cutting edge research, building the systems to put water back into the ground, and treating this for what it is: a generational challenge that demands a serious answer.

platform.value: Fight for a clear path to citizenship for law-abiding families, visa programs that meet labor needs, end to for-profit detention, and permanent protections for DREAMers
platform.snippet: Mark will fight for real reform. A clear path to citizenship for law-abiding families. Visa programs that meet the actual labor needs of our farms and industries. An end to for-profit detention. And permanent protections for DREAMers, because this is their country too.

platform.value: Make community college free and accessible, reduce student debt, restore federal research funding, protect international academic partnerships, and defend independence of educational institutions from political interference
platform.snippet: Mark will fight to make community college free and accessible to every American. He will push to reduce the crushing burden of student debt. He will restore federal research funding and protect the international academic partnerships that strengthen our universities and our economy. And he will defend the independence of our educational institutions from political interference.

bio_summary.value: Mark Nair is an educator, innovator, inventor, and entrepreneur running to be your voice in the United States House of Representatives. He, his wife, and his children have been part of the fabric of this district for more than 30 years.
